act: CSS Cascading and Inheritance Level 5 (Editor's Draft, 13 April 2026)

en.title: CSS Cascade 5: what does revert-rule roll back in a style attribute?
en.summary: §7.3.6 rolls revert-rule back “as if the current style rule had not been present”. §6.1 separates declarations in a style attribute from style rules, and §7.3.6 has a sentence for the animation origin but none for the style attribute. The same question for revert-layer was settled in issue 6743 with a dedicated sentence in §7.3.5. Browsers already agree on normal declarations: the web-platform-tests case for a style attribute passes in Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari with the 5px result (stable runs of 31 October 2026); no test covers !important.
en.impact: div { border-radius: 5px } and <div style="border-radius: 2px; border-radius: revert-rule">: if the whole attribute counts as the current rule the result is 5px; if only the declaration with revert-rule is removed it is 2px.
en.correction: Extend the §7.3.6 sentence “behaves like revert-layer in the animation origin” to element-attached styles, which matches the browser tests and brings in the §7.3.5 rule for important declarations.

quotes.source: CSS Cascading and Inheritance Level 5, Editor's Draft of 13 April 2026 (W3C CSS Working Group)
quotes.locator: §7.3.6 Rolling Back Rules: the revert-rule keyword
quotes.text: If the cascaded value of a property is the revert-rule keyword, the cascaded value is rolled back such that the specified value is calculated as if the current style rule had not been present at all.

quotes.source: CSS Cascading and Inheritance Level 5, Editor's Draft of 13 April 2026 (W3C CSS Working Group)
quotes.text: declarations that are attached directly to an element (such as the contents of a style attribute) rather than indirectly mapped by means of a style rule selector

quotes.source: CSS Cascading and Inheritance Level 5, Editor's Draft of 13 April 2026 (W3C CSS Working Group)
quotes.locator: §7.3.6 Rolling Back Rules: the revert-rule keyword
quotes.text: The revert-rule keyword behaves like revert-layer in the animation origin.
